name: Perla
description: Chef Lou Boquila turns the flavors of the Philippines into a refined, celebratory dining experience just off the Avenue. Rich, garlicky roast pork and bright, vinegary sides anchor a menu that helped put modern Filipino cooking on Philly's map.

name: The Dutch
description: This sunny corner spot has built a devoted following for its all-day brunch and comfort-driven American plates. Weekends bring long waits for pillowy French toast and hearty egg dishes served in a cheerful, casual room.

name: River Twice
description: Chef Randy Rucker runs an intimate, ever-changing tasting menu built around hyper-seasonal local ingredients and live-fire technique. The result is one of the neighborhood's most ambitious and creative fine-dining destinations.

name: Townsend
description: Chef Townsend Wentz delivers polished, classic French cooking in an elegant white-tablecloth setting on the Avenue. It remains a go-to for special occasions and one of South Philly's most accomplished upscale kitchens.

name: Mr. Martino's Trattoria
description: A charming, old-school South Philly trattoria open only a few nights a week, serving homemade pasta in a nostalgic, dimly lit room. The BYOB format and vintage feel make it a beloved throwback among locals.

name: Pizzata Pizzeria
description: This lively pizzeria fires up authentic Neapolitan-style pies with blistered, airy crusts and pairs them with a deep Italian beer list. It's a relaxed, family-friendly stop for wood-fired pizza on the Avenue.

name: Gabriella's Vietnam
description: This James Beard-recognized spot elevates Vietnamese cooking with dishes like delicate open-faced dumplings and whole fish steamed in a gourd. Warm hospitality and precise, vibrant flavors make it a standout on the strip.

name: Stargazy
description: Chef Sam Jacobson brings a taste of Britain to South Philly with hand-raised pork pies, Scotch eggs, and a hearty Sunday roast. The cozy shop is a one-of-a-kind destination for savory British classics.

name: Le Virtu
description: This destination for the rustic cuisine of Italy's Abruzzo region turns out hand-cut pastas and fire-grilled lamb skewers with serious authenticity. A lovely garden patio and deep regional wine list round out the experience.

name: El Chingon
description: A tiny, wildly popular BYOB known for its house-made sourdough tortillas and bold, from-scratch Mexican cooking. Standout tacos and the overstuffed cemita sandwich keep the line out the door.

name: Juana Tamale
description: Chef Jennifer Zavala's colorful, festive spot serves handmade tamales, birria tacos, and inventive Mexican street food with plenty of personality. Strong margaritas and a fun patio make it a neighborhood favorite.
